subject: Proposed Pay-As-You-Throw Waste Collection System
overview: City officials presented a revised solid waste proposal to maintain weekly trash pickup using existing carts alongside a subsidized Pay-As-You-Throw bag program, followed by extensive public comment. No implementation date was set pending review by the City Council and further community feedback.

items.title: Mayoral Remarks and Proposed Waste Collection Strategy
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn announced the city will not pursue bi-weekly trash collection and instead recommended maintaining weekly pickup with a subsidized Pay-As-You-Throw bag program projected to save $3.4 million over five years.

items.title: Environmental Background and State Waste Mandates
items.summary: Alicia Hunt outlined regional landfill capacity constraints, emissions and ash hazards from the Saugus incinerator, upcoming state bans on organic waste, and the need to divert the estimated 53 percent of trash that is recyclable or compostable.

items.title: Operational Options and Financial Comparison
items.summary: Commissioner McGivern presented operational comparisons among four collection models, explaining that retaining existing 64-gallon carts with official city-branded bags was the most cost-effective weekly option and qualified the city for state grant funding.

items.title: Composting Outreach and Compliance Technology
items.summary: Tyler Frank described ongoing curbside composting outreach and reviewed automated truck technologies, such as cameras and RFID sensors, capable of monitoring compliance without manual tagging.

items.title: Public Comment on Proposed Waste Operations
items.summary: Residents questioned bag capacity, multi-family unit allocations, potential costs after the initial year, surveillance methods, and illegal dumping, while expressing appreciation for preserving weekly collection.

items.title: Next Steps and Program Timeline
items.summary: Officials stated that public feedback will be compiled for review with the City Council in the new year, with no rollout occurring without advance community notice.
